doc.title: Paquito D'Rivera — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Bacalao con Pan and Irakere's early Egrem hits
summary: The band's first piece became an immediate Cuban hit and was followed by more Egrem releases; the group was very popular on the island.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Before you got the opportunity to make these tours to Eastern Europe and then to Jamaica, did the band record?

We recorded a piece that was an immediate success. It was a hit immediately, and that called “Bacalao con Pan.” Bacalaos con pan means, uh, Codfish with bread, and it was an immediate hit in, the hit parade in Cuba was that thing. So, we took it from there. There was a succession of hits, and the band became very popular in the island. Then in 1977, Dizzy Gillespie was there with Stan Getz with a group of musicians, on a cruise ship called The Daphne, and Earl Fatha Hines; it was a very impressive group of musicians. We didn’t know anything, because the newspapers say nothing, but we receive calls to present ourselves in the place and play with some American musicians. And then when they came back to New York, they talk about the group to Bruce Lundvall in CBS. And that was the way we become involved with CBS, and we recorded with CBS.
Now those early records, the ones you describe as making the Cuban hit parade, were they recorded for Egrem? Did you make an album for Egrem?
You made a few albums for Egrem?.

Yea, at least a couple of them, but that first one was a big success on the radio, you know that. I don’t remember the name of the other pieces, but “Bacalao Con Pan” was a boom, and they love that to dance.
